O filme brasileiro Eu Ainda Estou Aqui é uma obra que verdadeiramente merece ser laureada. O avanço da extrema-direita em diversas partes do mundo tem representado uma ameaça constante à arte e à cultura, pilares fundamentais da identidade e da memória coletiva de uma nação. Essa produção cinematográfica não apenas retrata com sensibilidade e profundidade os impactos do período em que essas forças estiveram no poder no Brasil, mas também evidencia a tentativa global de seu ressurgimento. Mais do que uma expressão artística ou uma realização cinematográfica de excelência, este filme representa uma necessária reparação histórica. A tragédia vivida pelo Brasil durante a ditadura militar (1964-1985) ainda ressoa na sociedade contemporânea, com marcas indeléveis na política, na educação e nas estruturas sociais. O filme, mesmo sem abarcar a totalidade dessa dolorosa realidade, cumpre um papel essencial ao trazer à tona um passado que muitos tentam apagar. A ditadura não apenas ceifou vidas e desestruturou famílias de todas as classes sociais, mas também promoveu um apagamento cultural e intelectual ao manipular currículos escolares e universitários, enfraquecendo a formação crítica das futuras gerações. Suas consequências ainda se fazem sentir, e o mundo precisa conhecer essa história. Diante disso, o reconhecimento desse filme pela Academia não seria apenas um tributo à sua qualidade artística, mas também um gesto de compromisso com a verdade histórica e com a memória dos que sofreram nesse período sombrio. Que a arte continue sendo um farol de resistência e esclarecimento. Que Eu Ainda Estou Aqui receba o reconhecimento que merece.

The Brazilian film I Am Still Here is a work that truly deserves to be honored. The rise of the far right in various parts of the world poses a constant threat to art and culture, which are fundamental pillars of a nation’s identity and collective memory. This film not only sensitively and profoundly portrays the impact of the period when these forces were in power in Brazil, but also highlights their global resurgence. More than just an artistic expression or a cinematic masterpiece, this film represents a necessary historical reckoning. The tragedy that Brazil endured during the military dictatorship (1964–1985) still echoes in contemporary society, leaving deep scars in politics, education, and social structures. While it cannot fully capture the extent of this painful reality, the film plays a crucial role in shedding light on a past that many try to erase. The dictatorship not only took lives and tore families apart across all social classes, but it also orchestrated cultural and intellectual suppression by manipulating school and university curricula, weakening the critical education of future generations. Its consequences are still felt today, and the world needs to know this history. Recognizing this film would not only be a tribute to its artistic excellence but also a commitment to historical truth and to the memory of those who suffered during this dark period. May art continue to be a beacon of resistance and enlightenment. May I Am Still Here receive the recognition it truly deserves.

The nomination of Ainda Estou Aqui in the categories of Best International Feature Film and Best Picture, along with Fernanda Torres’ nomination for Best Actress, represents one of the most significant moments for Brazilian cinema in Oscar history. At a time when the Academy is seeking to renew its image and expand its representation without falling into empty symbolic gestures, awarding Fernanda Torres and Ainda Estou Aqui would be a choice that unites artistic merit with genuine cultural impact. In recent years, the Oscars have been under pressure to reinvent themselves—whether to correct decades of exclusion of non-hegemonic voices or to respond to a global audience increasingly attentive to diverse cinematic narratives. However, this reinvention often stumbles into marketing strategies and a game of narrative that turns representation into a mere plot device. The power of Ainda Estou Aqui and Fernanda Torres’ performance lies precisely in their ability to transcend this game: this is not a film in the race solely because of its symbolic significance, but because it presents top-tier cinema—emotionally powerful and narratively sophisticated. Unlike recent cases where the Academy has tried to embrace the “new” without a solid artistic foundation, Ainda Estou Aqui asserts itself for what it is. Fernanda Torres’ visceral and complex performance aligns with a standard of excellence historically recognized by the Academy while broadening the scope of what it means to be a “Best Actress” in an Oscar race that still struggles against pre-established norms. Honoring Fernanda would not be an act of condescension or a superficial nod to the internationalization of the award but a genuine recognition of one of the most impactful performances of the year.

Moreover, Brazil’s presence in the Best Picture category reinforces the Academy’s need to connect with a new global cinema that does not rely exclusively on Hollywood or the traditional European circuit. Brazil, which has historically had an inconsistent presence at the Oscars, now arrives with a film that challenges labels and asserts itself based on its artistic value rather than external strategies. If the Academy truly wishes to redefine its significance in world cinema, awarding Ainda Estou Aqui and Fernanda Torres would be an authentic step in that direction—not as a narrative device for its own history but as a recognition of what cinema, in its purest essence, can achieve.
